events.title: Motorola Droid released
events.summary: Motorola released the Motorola Droid — Verizon Android flagship that popularized Android 2.0 in the US.
events.about: The phone expanded Android's flagship landscape beyond Samsung and Google. Verizon android flagship that popularized android 2.0 in the us.

narrative.whyChosen: The Motorola Droid was a significant Android flagship.
narrative.whyImportant: Diverse Android flagships gave developers multiple hardware targets beyond Galaxy and Pixel.
narrative.problemSolved: Android needed credible flagship alternatives to Samsung and carrier-skinned phones.

events.title: Go programming language open-sourced
events.summary: Google open-sourced Go on November 10, 2009 — a systems language from Pike, Thompson, and Griesemer with built-in concurrency.
events.about: Go targets cloud infrastructure: Docker, Kubernetes, Terraform, and countless microservices compile to single static binaries with goroutines for concurrency. It trades generics-era complexity (added later in Go 1.18) for fast compiles, a small language spec, and batteries-included networking in the standard library.

narrative.whyChosen: Go became the default language for cloud-native tooling and replaced C++ in many Google-scale services.
narrative.whyImportant: Goroutines and channels made concurrent servers approachable; fast builds changed how teams ship backend code.
narrative.problemSolved: C++ build times and complexity slowed Google infrastructure teams; they needed C-like speed with simpler concurrency.
